raw_response:
My reasoning:

I been farming this land 30 years. My father farmed it, my grandfather too. 6.5 mu, wheat then maize, same as everyone in our village. I do what worked last year because last year the harvest was alright.

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use the improved seed my neighbor Old Wang bought last year — he got good yield so I buy the same from the town dealer. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, the 15-15-15 kind, about one bag (50 jin, well, one sack) per mu when I sow. Then in spring when the wheat wakes up I spread urea, maybe half a bag per mu. My wife and I do it by hand, walking the rows. If I put less I worry the wheat will be yellow and thin, and then what? Better to put a little extra. A sack of urea is cheap compared to losing 100 jin of wheat.

I water the wheat maybe 3 times — before winter so roots don't dry, then in spring when it stands up, then when the grain is filling. I got the well, so water is not so expensive, just the electricity. I spray twice for the aphids and the yellow disease, whatever the dealer at the co-op says is going around this year.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, hybrid seed Zhengdan or whatever kind Old Wang got last year. I throw compound fertilizer in the furrow when I plant, and then topdress urea when the maize is knee-high. Summer rains come so I only irrigate once if July is dry. Maize don't need as much spraying as wheat, once for the borer.

I hire the tractor to rotary till — 40 yuan a mu, not worth breaking my back. My back already hurts.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 jin per mu, maize about 550. Same kind of year, I expect same.
